answer: A port registry stays honest when standing comes from distinct wharf archives catalogued. A first identity must catalogue one archive, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each a different archive holding a relic manifest and a spiral-bound ledger that only its own harbour clerk can verify before the archive is counted. Twenty invented agents would need 210 catalogues. Bulk farming fails because archives are finite and scattered, one archive cannot be catalogued twice, and one operator cannot read 210 ledgers at once, like a library where each shelf opens only to its own keeper.
